EQUANS
Equans is a world leader in the energy and services sector, with annual revenues of nearly €19,2 billion* and almost 800,000 projects.
Equans has leading positions in Europe, which is the result of the history of energy construction in these countries, and strong presences in North and South America and in Oceania.
With nearly 90,000 highly skilled employees, Equans has a strong geographic footprint, anchored by historic local brands. Equans provides its customers with excellent technical expertise in the design, installation, maintenance, and operation of multi-technical facilities. This know-how is based on key skills. First of all, in electrical and thermal engineering - two strong points that help accelerate the reduction of our clients' carbon footprint - but also in ventilation, refrigeration, mechanics and robotics, fire protection, energy renovation, digital solutions, IT, cyber security and telecommunications.
The combination of these expertises allows us to offer efficient and optimised solutions at all stages of the energy chain, from production, storage and transport to usage.
 (*) Turnover 2024 consolidated
 CTI ANALYST
Summary of the role
The CTI Analyst is a senior, business‑oriented cybersecurity intelligence professional responsible for producing high‑value threat intelligence to support executive decision‑making and defensive prioritization across the Group .
Embedded within the Active Defense CTI Pole , this role combines:
Strategic CTI, focused on long‑term threat assessment, business risk interpretation, and strategic foresight for executive leadership, and 
Tactical CTI, focused on translating threat intelligence into clear defensive priorities for security stakeholders. 
 While remaining strictly non ‑ operational (no IOC handling, no real‑time incident response - these are handled by the CSIRT Threat Management).
 Strategic stakeholders
Executive leadership (COMEX) 
Group & Entity CISOs 
Growth and M&A leadership (cyber due diligence) 
 Tactical stakeholders
CSIRT / Threat Management 
Offensive Security 
Vulnerability Operation Center 
Group & Entity CISOs (in their defensive leadership role) 
 The role translates complex cyber threats into clear, actionable insights that influence:
Strategic priorities and investments 
Risk appetite and governance decisions 
Defensive focus areas and security roadmaps 
Acquisition and integration decisions 
 in line with the Group cyber strategy and exposure management objectives.
 Key Responsibilities
 Executive Level Threat Intelligence & Decision Support (Strategic)
Produce high level strategic threat intelligence tailored for executive audiences (COMEX). 
Identify macro trends, structural shifts, and long term threat scenarios impacting business operations, reputation, and growth. 
Assess likelihood, impact, and risk trajectories across geographies, sectors, and Group activities. 
Provide decision oriented recommendations supporting prioritization, investment decisions, and risk tolerance. 
 Strategic & Tactical Threat Landscape for CISOs and Security Leadership
Deliver sector based and geographic threat landscapes aligned with EQUANS’ activities, value chains, and exposure. 
Analyze threat actors and ecosystems: 
Cybercrime and ransomware groups 
State sponsored actors 
Hacktivist and hybrid threat actors 
Translate strategic intelligence into tactical threat understanding by: 
Analyzing adversary TTPs and attack patterns 
Mapping threat behavior against Group relevant attack surfaces 
Map threats against key security domains: 
Identity & Access 
Cloud & data 
Supply chain & third parties 
Support CISOs in defining: 
Multi year security roadmaps 
Control priorities 
Defensive focus areas grounded in real threat activity 
 Tactical CTI: Defense Prioritization for Security Teams
 This responsibility explicitly supports CSIRT, Offensive Security, Vulnerability Management, and CISOs.
Provide tactical threat intelligence to guide defensive prioritization across the cyberdefense functions. 
Analyze: 
Adversary kill chains and exploitation paths 
Exploitation velocity and campaign maturity 
Threat relevance to Group exposure and asset criticality 
Translate threat intelligence into clear tactical priorities for: 
Vulnerability Management 
CSIRT / Threat Management 
Offensive Security 
CISOs 
Contribute to exposure driven decision making across: 
Vulnerability management 
External attack surface management (EASM) 
Security control reinforcement 
 M&A Cyber Due Diligence & Strategic Investigations
Conduct cyber risk assessments of acquisition targets based on: 
External exposure and attack surface indicators 
Public incident history and breach signals 
Apparent security posture and technical debt 
Integrate tactical threat signals (sector targeting, active exploitation trends, known adversary interest) into due diligence analysis. 
Identify strategic and tactical red flags affecting valuation, integration risk, and post‑acquisition security effort. 
Produce executive‑level due diligence notes and risk summaries. 
 Strategic & Tactical Deliverables & Reporting
Produce and maintain key CTI outputs: 
Executive Threat Briefs (monthly / quarterly) 
Strategic & Tactical Threat Landscape Reports 
M&A / Due Diligence Cyber Notes 
Position papers on emerging and actively exploited threats 
Ensure intelligence products are: 
Decision‑oriented 
Actionable for security leadership 
Clearly adapted to executive vs defensive audiences 
 CTI Governance, Interfaces & Alignment
Contribute to the definition and maintenance of the corporate CTI editorial line: 
Key messages 
Intelligence priorities 
Target audiences 
Standardize formats for executive and security leadership consumption. 
Act as the strategic and tactical interface with the CSIRT Threat Management 
Consume ground‑level intelligence to produce: 
Strategic synthesis for executives 
Tactical prioritization for security teams 
Ensure continuous alignment between: 
Observed threat activity 
Defensive priorities 
Group cyber strategy 
 PROFILE
 Experience
Minimum of 5 years’ experience as a Threat Intelligence analyst 
Proven exposure to executive‑level reporting and stakeholder engagement. 
Experience with: 
Strategic cyber risk analysis 
Tactical threat analysis (TTPs, exploitation trends) 
Business impact assessment or cyber due diligence is strongly valued. 
Prior work in consulting, large enterprises, or critical infrastructure environments is a plus. 
 Core Skills
Strong ability to translate technical threats into business and strategic language. 
Analytical mindset with structured reasoning (probability, impact, scenarios). 
Excellent written communication skills for C‑level and Board audiences. 
Solid understanding of: 
Cyber threat ecosystems 
Ransomware and cybercrime economics 
State‑sponsored and geopolitical cyber risks 
 Soft Skills
Strategic thinker with a long‑term vision of cyber risk. 
Credible, calm, and impactful when interacting with senior leadership. 
High standards of rigor, clarity, and relevance. 
Collaborative, able to work across entities and discipline 
Ability to operate autonomously and manage sensitive topics with discretion. 
 Why Join Us?
Global Impact: Influence identity governance across a multinational company. 
Challenging Projects: Work on cutting-edge IGA initiatives with real business impact. 
Career Growth: Opportunity to evolve into IAM leadership or architecture roles. 
Collaborative Culture: Work with experts in cybersecurity, cloud, and compliance.
